title: Floating-equations animated background effect (personal brand, #202020 tint)
description:
Port the "floating equations sliding across a dark background" visual effect
from the talkinghead video-content repo to this site as a background/hero
effect, using David's own equations (math/finance/physics/computer science),
tinted #202020 (the same dark charcoal used as the video pipeline's personal
background color).

REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION (read before designing, don't reinvent):
- /Users/david/Projects/WORK/CONSULTING/content-tools/talkinghead/src/subutils/equation_effect.py
  — create_equation_overlay(): loads a set of transparent PNG/SVG equation
  assets, recolors them to a single tint color, and slides each one across
  the frame on its own randomized diagonal path/timing, with collision
  avoidance against reserved zones (e.g. keeps clear of a watermark corner).
- /Users/david/Projects/WORK/CONSULTING/content-tools/talkinghead/src/tools/back_bumper_2.py
  — the original consumer (a personal-brand video bumper); shows the visual
  in motion (outputs/bumpers/personal/back_2.mp4 in that repo).
- /Users/david/Projects/WORK/CONSULTING/content-tools/talkinghead/src/tools/audio_backdrop_generator.py
  — a second consumer that reuses the same effect for arbitrary-length
  animated video backgrounds (a newer, more general wrapper worth reading
  for how it composes with other layers).
- Equation assets themselves: src/static/images/equation_assets/*.png (+ one
  .svg) in that same repo — these are pre-rendered PNG images of specific
  equations (Euler's identity, F=ma, Pythagorean theorem, etc.), NOT
  rendered from LaTeX at runtime. For the web port, decide whether to reuse
  these as static image assets (fast, simple, matches video branding
  exactly) or re-render the same equation SET as SVG/MathML/KaTeX for
  crisper scaling on the web (probably the better call for a website, but
  is a real design decision, not a given — do the reference reading before
  choosing).

WEB PORT SCOPE:
1. Define a JSON (or TS const) config: an array of "beloved equations" in
   math/finance/physics/computer science that David wants floating in the
   background. David has not yet supplied this list — either ask him for it
   directly, or draft a reasonable starter set (e.g. E=mc^2, F=ma, Euler's
   identity, Black-Scholes, Kelly criterion, Shannon entropy, Bayes'
   theorem, P vs NP) and confirm with him before treating it as final.
2. Build a background/hero component (this is an Astro site — check
   src/components/ and src/layouts/ for the existing component conventions;
   no background/hero effect component exists yet as of 2026-08-23) that
   renders that equation set sliding across the viewport, recolored to
   #202020, mirroring the reference implementation's slow-drift/randomized-
   path feel rather than inventing a new animation language.
3. Decide the rendering approach (CSS animations on static SVG/image
   elements vs. canvas vs. a small JS animation loop) based on this site's
   existing stack (Astro + whatever's already in package.json — check
   before adding a new animation/canvas dependency; prefer zero new deps if
   the existing stack already covers it).
4. Respect this site's existing perf/accessibility bars: this is a
   Lighthouse-scored site (see AstroPaper-lighthouse-score.svg in repo
   root) — an animated background must not tank Lighthouse performance
   score or violate prefers-reduced-motion; add a reduced-motion fallback
   (static or no animation) as part of the initial implementation, not a
   follow-up.
5. Where it lands (homepage hero, a specific page, sitewide layout
   background) is David's call — ask/confirm before assuming sitewide.

Not scoped here: any changes to the talkinghead repo's own equation effect
code — this is a one-way port of the VISUAL CONCEPT to a completely
different codebase/stack (Astro/TS static site vs. Python/moviepy video
pipeline), not a shared-code refactor between the two repos.
notes:
[Update: fixed a real bug David caught by eye — equations were restarting on every page navigation]

David flagged: floating-equation animations shouldn't get interrupted by page changes; they're
in the base layout so that should just work. Checked empirically rather than assuming — and he
was right, it was NOT working: `transition:persist` alone did not keep the #floating-equations
element across an Astro ClientRouter (astro:transitions) navigation. Tested by clicking an
internal link and diffing the DOM node identity + each equation's inline style (position/speed/
size) before vs after: the container was a DIFFERENT node and every equation had re-randomized,
i.e. the whole field visibly reset on every page change.

Root cause: `transition:persist` without an explicit `transition:name` doesn't reliably match the
outgoing/incoming element as the same persisted element across two independently-server-rendered
pages (each page's FloatingEquations.astro reruns its own Math.random() calls at render time, so
without a stable match key Astro just treats them as unrelated and swaps normally).

Fix: added `transition:name="floating-equations"` alongside `transition:persist` on the container
div. Re-tested the same way: container node now IS the same DOM node after navigation, and every
equation's style values are byte-identical before/after — the animation now genuinely continues
uninterrupted across page changes instead of restarting.

Full re-validation after this fix: astro check 0 errors, astro build 114 pages, vitest 258/258
passed (the previously-flaky yarn-build-dependent suite is now passing too — that was a transient
machine/corepack issue, not something in this diff).

title: Permafix dev-server warnings: KaTeX math-mode content bugs + Vite fs.allow symlink rejection
description:
Running `yarn dev` (or `astro dev`) in this repo (or any of its git worktrees) floods the console
with two unrelated categories of warnings/errors. Both have real root causes and should be fixed
at the source, not suppressed with a --quiet flag or a try/catch around the logger.

CATEGORY 1: KaTeX "LaTeX-incompatible input" warnings from remark-math/rehype-katex
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Content authors wrapped non-math prose (Arabic text, Chinese text, curly smart quotes, a literal
percent character, zero-width spaces) inside dollar-sign inline-math delimiters in blog post
markdown. KaTeX then tries to parse that prose as LaTeX math and either emits a strict-mode
warning (kept non-fatal by remark-math's default strict:'warn') or renders it wrong ("No character
metrics for '...' in style 'Main-Regular'" means those glyphs get badly-kerned/mispositioned
output, not just a console warning -- this is a real rendering bug on the built page, not only a
build-log annoyance).

Confirmed culprits found by grep (there may be more -- do a thorough pass, this list is a starting
point, not exhaustive):
  - src/content/blog/ar/ark-capacitor-ar.md -- Arabic prose wrapped in math delimiters
  - src/content/blog/Is-the-soul-a-physical-part-of-you.md -- a literal percent character inside a
    math span, which LaTeX/KaTeX treats as "start of comment", producing the
    "comment has no terminating newline" warning
  - src/content/blog/The-Discrete-Expectation-of-good.md -- curly quotes inside a math span
  - Chinese-language warnings (that book, left/right, etc.) were also seen in the dev-server log
    but the source could NOT be pinned down via a quick grep of src/content (there is no
    src/content/blog/zh directory -- the zh output is likely produced by a build-time
    translation/i18n step, not a raw markdown file). Find where that Chinese text actually
    originates (check src/i18n/, src/utils/ for a translation/localization pipeline, and
    src/pages/zh/**) and trace why the math delimiters survived translation while carrying
    non-math prose inside them.

PERMAFIX, not suppress: fix the actual markdown/content source (remove the math delimiters around
prose that isn't math, escape the literal percent character, replace curly quotes with straight
quotes or move them outside the math span, and fix whatever step produces the zh content) so a
real astro build run has zero KaTeX strict-mode warnings. Do not just set strict:false in the
remark-math config or pipe stderr through a filter -- that hides real rendering bugs on the live
pages, it doesn't fix them.

CATEGORY 2: Vite "outside of Vite serving allow list" errors in dev mode
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
astro dev (equivalently yarn dev) spams repeated errors for every self-hosted font file
(fontsource IBM Plex fonts, KaTeX fonts) and the dev-toolbar entrypoint, of the form:
  [ERROR] [vite] The request url ".../node_modules/@fontsource/.../*.woff2" is
  outside of Vite serving allow list.
This happens specifically when running from a git worktree (e.g. .worktrees/davidaw_ad-292) whose
node_modules is a SYMLINK to the main checkout's real node_modules directory (readlink node_modules
points at the parent repo root) -- Vite's default server.fs.allow restricts served files to the
project root and doesn't automatically follow a symlink whose resolved realpath escapes that root,
so every font/asset actually stored in the shared node_modules gets rejected even though the site
otherwise renders fine (browsers fall back silently, so this is invisible in the UI but fills the
terminal with noise on every dev session in every worktree).

There is currently no vite.server.fs config at all in astro.config.mjs. PERMAFIX: add the resolved
real repo root to astro.config.mjs's vite.server.fs.allow array (e.g. via
fs.realpathSync(path.join(process.cwd(), 'node_modules'))), so this works cleanly from the main
checkout AND from every worktree without per-worktree config. Verify by running astro dev, loading
the homepage, and confirming zero "outside of Vite serving allow list" lines in the terminal
output.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. astro build produces zero KaTeX strict-mode warnings in its output.
2. astro dev, loaded homepage + at least one post with math + the /ar/ and /zh/ variants of the
   affected pages, produces zero "outside of Vite serving allow list" lines.
3. Visually confirm (via BrowserOS or similar) that the previously-mis-rendered math (the Arabic
   and percent-sign and curly-quote cases) now renders correctly, not just "warning-free" -- a
   build that's silent but still visually wrong doesn't satisfy this bead.
4. astro check and vitest run still pass with no new regressions.
5. This is unrelated to the davidaw_ad-292 floating-equations bead -- do not touch
   src/components/FloatingEquations.astro, src/data/equations.ts, or src/layouts/Layout.astro
   unless a genuine conflict is found (unlikely; these are content + vite-config fixes).
notes:
STATUS: Fixed for real (config + content changes), not suppressed. Full verification below.

What happened: the dispatched subagent did solid, correct diagnostic + fix work (astro.config.mjs
Vite fs.allow fix + 10 markdown content fixes across en/ar/zh mirrors) but got cut off by an
account-wide Claude session usage limit right as it started its own final verification pass
(external resource constraint, unrelated to this codebase). I picked up from there, independently
verified every change it made file-by-file, found and fixed one remaining bug it hadn't caught, and
reran the full verification suite myself.

CATEGORY 1 FIX (KaTeX warnings) -- confirmed correct, all content-level, no suppression:
- src/content/blog/Is-the-soul-a-physical-part-of-you.md: removed bogus `$...$` math delimiters
  around a plain "60%" that isn't math.
- src/content/blog/NWCU.md (+ src/data/blog/en mirror): escaped literal `$16,000` / `$12,000` /
  `$0.10` / `$180` dollar amounts to `\$...` so they don't get misread as opening math mode.
- src/content/blog/The-Discrete-Expectation-of-good.md (+ en mirror): moved curly-quoted "good"
  inside `\text{"good"}` instead of raw curly-quote characters directly in math mode.
- src/data/blog/en/why-quantum-gravity-is-unrenormalizable.md (+ zh mirror): fixed
  `A_x​,A_y​,A_z​` -- this had a zero-width space (U+200B) after each variable AND was missing
  underscore-subscript syntax; now correctly `A_x,A_y,A_z`, a real rendering fix not just a
  warning fix.
- src/data/blog/ar/why-quantum-gravity-is-unrenormalizable-ar.md: KaTeX's Main-Regular font has no
  Arabic glyph metrics at all, so Arabic text can never render correctly inside a `\text{}` math
  annotation -- translated the math-mode labels (previously Arabic) to English/Latin inside the
  equations, and added a short parenthetical Arabic gloss just outside the math for context. This
  is a real font-capability constraint, not a workaround: no LaTeX/KaTeX Arabic font exists that
  makes this work any other way.
- I FOUND AND FIXED (the subagent had not caught this one): src/content/blog/ark-capacitor.md,
  src/content/blog/ar/ark-capacitor-ar.md, src/data/blog/en/ark-capacitor.md, and
  src/data/blog/ar/ark-capacitor-ar.md all had `$ \( C = 1 \, \mu\text{F} \)$  and $\( V = 10^6 \,
  \text{V} \) $` -- a redundant LaTeX `\(...\)` inline-math delimiter nested INSIDE an
  already-open remark-math `$...$` delimiter, which KaTeX cannot parse (produces a real red
  "katex-error" span on the live page, not just a console warning). Removed the redundant `\(`/`\)`
  pairs in all 4 files.

CATEGORY 2 FIX (Vite fs.allow) -- confirmed correct:
- astro.config.mjs: resolves `node_modules`'s realpath via `fs.realpathSync` and adds both the
  project root and that realpath to `vite.server.fs.allow`. Works correctly whether node_modules
  is real (main checkout) or a symlink (any worktree) -- no hardcoded worktree-specific path.

FULL VERIFICATION (all re-run by me after picking up from the subagent, from a clean state):
- `astro build`: 0 KaTeX strict-mode warnings in the full build log (previously dozens per build).
- Full-output grep for `katex-error` across every built page: 0 hits (previously 2 pages with a
  visibly broken red error span -- the ark-capacitor bug above).
- `astro dev`, loaded homepage + /ar/ + /zh/ + the math-heavy ark-capacitor post via real HTTP
  requests: 0 "outside of Vite serving allow list" lines in the dev server log (previously ~20+
  per page load, for every fontsource/KaTeX font file and the dev-toolbar entrypoint).
- `astro check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 pre-existing unrelated hint.
- `vitest run`: 258/258 tests passed.
- Confirmed `public/` build output is gitignored and untracked (not an issue the subagent needed
  to worry about).
- Confirmed no changes to src/components/FloatingEquations.astro, src/data/equations.ts, or
  src/layouts/Layout.astro (the unrelated davidaw_ad-292 bead's files) -- clean separation held.

Not committed -- awaiting go-ahead per this repo's conservative git profile.

title: Add regression tests for FloatingEquations (equation validity + reduced-motion)
description:
Follow-up from adversarial review of davidaw_ad-292 (sitewide floating equations background).

Two verification gaps were caught by manual/one-time checks during that bead but have no
automated regression coverage, so a future change could silently reintroduce them:

1. src/data/equations.ts entries are rendered via katex.renderToString(latex, {throwOnError: false}).
   throwOnError:false means a malformed LaTeX string added later would silently degrade to a
   red .katex-error span instead of failing the build. Add a unit test that iterates
   FLOATING_EQUATIONS and asserts katex.renderToString(latex, {throwOnError: true}) does not throw
   for every entry.

2. The prefers-reduced-motion fallback in src/components/FloatingEquations.astro (freeze in place at
   each equation's own --static-left, no shared position) has zero test coverage — nothing currently
   fails if a future refactor drops that CSS block or reverts to a single shared static offset.
   Consider a Playwright test (this repo already has @playwright/test configured) that emulates
   prefers-reduced-motion: reduce and asserts floating-equation elements have distinct computed
   transform/left values rather than one shared value.

Not urgent — the current behavior is correct and manually verified as of davidaw_ad-292; this is
about preventing silent regression, not fixing a live bug.
